questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
An international environment that is easy to adjust into. 
Amsterdam is a big student city with many universities that offers English-speaking educations, this attracks many internationals to the city. This, among other things, makes it an interesting city to stay in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed my stay in Amsterdam, but there was a lot of problems with getting my courses pre-approved and the process before-hand made me feel insecure about my exchange and caused some problems with choosing courses at my host university. 
Especially because my pre-approval ended up taking so long the process went on into the summervacation, where the wait for approval was very long. This was a very stressful situation for me and I think it affected my start on exchange and my ability to find a place to stay and settle in. 
However, my experience on exchange was really good, and the host university was very helpful and informative.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The host university was very informative and gave very detailed information on intro-week and the first weeks at the university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got some assistance with my course-selection, as I was a bit delayed in that process due to my pre-approval being very delayed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
They always answered within a day and had a team of three people only working with exchange students. This made me feel very comfortable at the university and I was always able to addres any type of concern. 
Additionally they had office hours where exchange students could come and ask questions at the university. 
They have been extremely helpful and understanding.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was hard to find housing in Amsterdam, as they are experiencing a housing crisis at the moment. 
I found my first studio on Instagram, because I already had a small network in Amsterdam before arriving. This studio was very far away from campus, and I ended up moving in with fellow exchange students in an apartment closer to campus after two months.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is hard to find and expensive. However, it is duable and also a fun way to get to meet people and live. I was very happy with the place I ended up living and through the people I lived with there I met a lot of other people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The university only had very limited housing opportunities and I was originally signed up the housing through the university, but it was all "sold out" after 10 minutes. 
I wish the university would have had more student housing to offer, as this would have been a lot less stressful. However, I ended up being very happy with where I was living.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I signed up for a lot of courses (more than necessary) due to problems woth my pre-approval at my home university and therefore I did not know which ones I should sign up for. 
However, my home university was very helpful and I was able to choose courses that I might de-register from. I think the host university was extremely helpful due to my situation.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was able to get help over the phone and e-mail and also face-to-face.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the courses I wanted, but due to problems with my pre-approval I was not able to register for all of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They are very helpful at Vrije Universiteit, so just ask them if you have any concerns.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the academic level was okay. However, I think some of the classes was lacking a little bit of "depth" and was a little too general.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more contact with the professors. Some of my classes was a bit smaller and invited the students to engage more active in the courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a movie theater on campus, a sport center, many restaurants and bars.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I did not participate in many activities on campus, as many of my friends did not live on campus but lived in the city. Therefore, most of the acitivities I would recommend are there. 
I would recommend getting a Museumkaart. You pay 60 euros and then you have access to all museums in the Netherlands for a year. I used that a lot as Amsterdam has many museums. 
I would also recommend visiting Bimhuis on Tuesday evenings. Here the students at the conservatory give free jazz concerts. This is a very fun event with a lot of other students and a cheap bar. It normally lasts till 1 am. 
I would also recommend going to the OBA libraries to study. They normally have a lot of good study-spots with nice views and good (cheap) coffee. 
In the fall they also have an event called Museumnacht, which is similar to the Danish Kulturnat. Here all the museums are open during the night and some of them almost turn into night clubs. 
About once a month there is also a fleamarket in IJhallen in Noord. This is the biggest fleamarket in Europe and is a very fun activity to due. 
I would definitely recommend going to Noord and experience that part of the town. It is a lesser known part of the city, but very fun and diverse.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
The same as above. I would also recommend visiting some of the other cities close to Amsterdam such as Leiden, Rotterdam, Utrecht, Haag and Haarlem. These cities are all very accessible and fun to see. 
I also rented a car for a day with some friends and drove through some of the country-side North of Amsterdam. I would definitely recommend that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. The Netherlands is different than Denmark, but I would argue that as a Dane it is not hard to adjust to the culture at a Dutch university.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in the introduction week.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were very little, but I did find another work-ethic with the people I met on exchange, and the Dutch people tend to be a bit more direct in my opinion.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The welcomming of internationals and the willingness to speak English and include other cultures. I think the Netherlands was very including and as an international it was easy to adjust.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Participate in the introduction week. Personally I did not like the activies planned there and I do not think it was very good planned. However, this was where I met my best friends on exchange. 
Participate actively in the lectures and classes. I got a newfound academic confidence boost from engaging a lot with the classes, and they really create an evironment where this is possible. 
Explore Amsterdam and all of its beautiful cultural activities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It is important to note that you need to be registered with the municipality. This is very important when finding a place to live, because of the big housing crisis there are many places where you can live but where the landlord do not let you register. 
This is illegal and can cause you a lot of problems. Therefore it is important to check beforehand if you can register at the address.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Creating a new home that feels like home, knowing that you will leave it soon.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
